order: Apply the round-three findings from the owner-requested holistic review. First, strike the seven-day maxStaleMs ruled in round one and replace it with a forty-eight-hour ceiling — a weekly allowance moves too fast for a week-old reading to count as evidence — while the 24-hour maxFreshMs window stands as ruled. Second, carry the staleness disclosure onto the published bucket-state object, adding stale and ageMs keys, so a snapshot consumer or the dispatcher sees what the human report already shows. Third, ledger the outstanding exercise debt and commit the round-three verdicts and band records. Make the disclosure purely additive. Staleness is disclosed, not discounted — publish the recorded fraction exactly as read, leave reserveBreached, throttleObserved and exhausted computed the way they are today, and let no bucket's routed pool state change merely because its reading is stale. Do not modify router/router.js; the router keeps ownership of the ladder and the reserve formula.
claims: The ceiling moves to forty-eight hours and the fresh window is untouched. The only additions to the published state object are the stale and ageMs keys; its routing-relevant fields are computed exactly as before, so no bucket's routed pool state moves because a reading is stale, and router/router.js was not opened. Round-three verdicts, band records and the outstanding exercise debt are committed. Verified with node tests/quartermaster.test.js, 191 passed, and node tests/router.test.js, 135 passed.
